sources.entry: Jellystat | Statistics and monitoring for Jellyfin

summary.one_liner: Jellystat is a free, open source statistics and monitoring app for Jellyfin (with Emby support), backed by Postgres, that tracks playback sessions, watch history and library/user statistics.
summary.what_it_does: Monitors Jellyfin sessions and logs them, and produces statistics for all libraries and users. It keeps a watch history and per-user overview and activity, plus watch statistics. It can back up and restore its data, automatically sync library items, and integrate with the Jellyfin Statistics Plugin. Configuration is done through environment variables, including Postgres connection settings, a JWT secret, optional MaxMind GeoLite credentials for IP geolocation, and a minimum playback length filter. The README notes that Emby can be used by setting IS_EMBY_API. Swagger API docs are served at /swagger.
use_cases: Track who watched what on a Jellyfin server
View per-user and per-library viewing statistics
Back up and restore media server statistics data
Geolocate viewer IP addresses for playback logs
how_to_run: Set environment variables (see Environmental Variables table; POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_IP, POSTGRES_PORT, JWT_SECRET, and TZ are required)
Run `npm run start-app` to run backend and frontend together (or `npm run start-server` / `npm run start-client` separately)
For Docker, see the DockerHub reference in the README (no command given)
notable: Session monitoring plus watch history and per-user activity for Jellyfin
Docker secrets support through FILE__ prefixed environment variables
caveats: README says the project is still in development and expect some weirdness
Author has announced a full rebuild with a new backend, frontend and possibly new database, and says the current project will not be updated for a while apart from major bug fixes
Responsive UI and multi-server support are listed as required development but not yet done
